claims.text: The high-entropy film has the composition LaCr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Co0.2Ni0.2O3–δ.
High-entropy perovskite oxide films have enhanced OER activity relative to analogous single-B-site perovskite oxide films.
Dynamic interplay among diverse B-site transition-metal cations causes the enhanced OER activity.
The diversity of B-site cations creates transient multicationic active ensembles.
Transient multicationic active ensembles optimize the adsorption of oxygen intermediates.
Transient multicationic active ensembles lower OER energy barriers relative to single-B-site perovskite oxides.
Co-localization of diverse transition-metal cations in the high-entropy structure produces a multicationic active-site ensemble.
Dynamic redox interplay among the different B-site ions facilitates simultaneous oxidation-state shifts during oxygen-intermediate adsorption.
The simultaneous oxidation-state shifts lower reaction barriers.
The simultaneous oxidation-state shifts promote faster OER kinetics than occur in single-B-site films.
High-entropy films will exhibit markedly higher OER current density than single-B-site films.
High-entropy films will exhibit improved OER kinetics relative to single-B-site films.
Operando spectroscopy will reveal coupled, rapid redox transitions in the high-entropy films during OER.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply to epitaxially grown perovskite oxides operating in aqueous OER environments.
The proposed mechanism may not extend to catalysts with different morphologies or reaction environments.
Subtle differences in film quality could influence the measured OER and spectroscopic responses.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome field says that either failure to observe dynamic redox changes or absence of enhanced OER performance would falsify the hypothesis, whereas the formal falsification rule requires both absent enhancement and absent redox shifts. These are different logical criteria.
